message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and ensure safe, habitable housing. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes. This is not legal advice; if you have a specific dispute, consult a qualified attorney. | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | Keep records of the unit’s condition at move‑in and move‑out. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition. | Report repairs promptly; landlords cannot refuse to fix major issues. | | **Rent Increases** | • No limit on how much rent can increase, but it must be in writing and given at least 30 days’ notice before the new amount takes effect. | If you’re a month‑to‑month tenant, a 30‑day notice is required. | | **Lease Termination** | • Landlord must give at least 30 days’ written notice to terminate a month‑to‑month lease.
• For fixed‑term leases, landlord may only terminate for cause (e.g., nonpayment, violation of lease). | Tenants can also terminate with 30 days’ notice. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot interfere with your peaceful use of the property. | Landlords cannot enter without proper notice (usually 24 hours) unless emergency. | | **Notice of Entry** | • Landlord must give at least 24 hours’ written notice before entering, except in emergencies. | Landlords cannot repeatedly enter without notice. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., Section 8). | Fair Housing Act applies to all rental properties. | | **Repair and Deduct / Rent Withholding** | • If landlord fails to repair major problems, tenant may pay the repair cost and deduct from rent, or withhold rent until repaired. | Must follow proper procedure: give notice, allow reasonable time to repair, keep receipts. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment, 30‑day notice for lease termination).
• Eviction must go through court; landlord cannot forcibly remove tenant. | Tenants can contest eviction in court. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord cannot conduct surveillance or tamper with tenant’s personal belongings. | Landlords must respect tenant privacy. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide water, heat, and electricity unless otherwise specified. | Tenants can’t be forced to pay for utilities that are part of the lease. | | **Subletting / Assignment** | • Tenants may sublet or assign lease with landlord’s consent, which cannot be unreasonably withheld. | Landlords can’t arbitrarily deny subletting. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlord must keep common areas clean and safe. | Tenants can report maintenance issues. | | **Legal Remedies** | • Tenants can sue for breach of contract, damages, or seek injunctive relief. | Tenants can recover actual damages, attorney fees, and court costs. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Read the Lease Carefully** – Understand what is required of both parties. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of notices, emails, repair requests, and photos of the unit. 3. **Use Written Notices** – Send all communications via certified mail or email with read receipts. 4. **Know the Notice Periods** – 24‑hour notice for entry, 30‑day notice for rent increases or lease termination. 5. **Report Problems Promptly** – Provide written notice of needed repairs and keep a copy. 6. **Seek Legal Help Early** – If you receive a notice of eviction or notice of non‑payment, contact a lawyer or tenant advocacy group. ### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – Provides consumer rights guides. - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** – Offers resources on fair housing. - **Local Tenant Advocacy Groups** – Many cities have nonprofits that help tenants with disputes. - **Legal Aid Organizations** – Provide free or low‑cost legal assistance. --- If you have a specific situation—such as a notice of eviction, a dispute over a security deposit, or a landlord refusing to make repairs—please let me know, and I can offer more tailored guidance or help draft a letter to your landlord.
